correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and long northward ice-side approach
correspondence.finding: The opening lies on mapped Inland Ice west of Lambert Land. Its long northward stretch and short eastward/northeastward steps remain in the western ice-margin corridor toward the southern end of Kronprins Christian Land. The sheet distinguishes this light-blue ice/perennial-snow terrain from the adjacent exposed bedrock. No source label establishes these modeled steps as a named natural river.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Full ordinary corridor-scale setting covered. Ice-surface contours are not interpreted as a river trace or subglacial drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern continuation and eastward bend through the Skallingen setting
correspondence.finding: The northward continuation reaches the southern Kronprins Christian Land margin and the eastward bend occupies the exposed-rock and valley setting of Skallingen. The following southward steps approach its southern margin. The source shows geological/terrain units, superficial-deposit valleys and local ice or snow, rather than a continuously named river matching the entire modeled bend.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The terrain and connecting geographic settings are read from the original sheet. A regional land name is not a hydronym, and geological boundaries or fault traces are not adopted as channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward transition into Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden
correspondence.finding: The southeastward sequence leaves the southern Skallingen/Kap Steglich-Petersen setting and enters the ice-covered Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden corridor separating that land from Lambert Land. Blåsø is separately mapped to the west of this transition; it is not assigned as a selected through-lake segment, nor used to infer an unseen river connection. No lake or fjord label licenses naming the whole modeled route.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The connector is geographically covered. The historical map distinguishes the lake, land and ice-covered fjord setting; present hydrological continuity or flow direction is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward crossing of Lambert Land
correspondence.finding: The next southward and southeastward intervals reach northwestern Lambert Land, then continue through its mapped ice/perennial-snow areas, exposed bedrock and superficial-deposit corridors toward the southern margin. All of the long descending connector is within the original sheet. No natural-river name or named tributary system is established across these different settings.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: These are source-setting observations at generalized component scale, not exact banks, a surveyed channel, a claim that every short modeled step follows a real river, or an inferred subglacial route.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern approach, eastward final reach and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The southern approach reaches the Kap Zachariae vicinity on Lambert Land and the final eastward interval ends immediately east of that cape, on the northern side of the historical mapped Zachariae Isstrøm ice/coastal setting. The source separates this ending from the Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden corridor farther north. Jøkelbugten, labeled farther south on the sheet, is not asserted as the selected terminal. No terminal fjord name is assigned by proximity.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The actual ending is read at ordinary terminal-corridor scale. The retained model class sea is metadata, not proof of a current surveyed mouth or ice front. This 2000 sheet does not establish contemporary shoreline or glacier-front positions.

correspondence.component_scope: Western headward branch
correspondence.finding: The selected western start corresponds at generalized scale to the southern of the west-starting headward branches east of Missisa Lake. The printed index traces this branch eastward and then northeast toward the Lawashi corridor. The branch itself is not labelled with a hydronym. No source-lake name or surveyed source point is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper branch junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected headward branch passes through the mapped confluence pattern south of the Lawashi label and joins the more northerly labelled Lawashi corridor. The neighbouring northerly branch and other tributaries are kept distinct from the selected initial feeder; no nearby label is propagated across all upstream reaches.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Central northeastward continuation
correspondence.finding: The map supplies a continuous northeastward river corridor from the upper confluence area through the central lowland, south of the Attawapiskat system and north of the separately labelled Kapiskau system. The long northeastward trend, intervening tributary junctions and change to the lower easterly reach correspond to the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower easterly bend and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The mapped Lawashi corridor bends east and southeast before turning northeast toward James Bay. The river remains geographically distinct from Kapiskau and its associated southern tributaries. Adjacent small waterbodies are not assigned to the selected route merely because they are nearby.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern connecting channel and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Near the coastal end, the map shows a southern connection from the Attawapiskat channel system entering the selected lower river before its James Bay outlet. The selected terminal is the coastal outlet southeast of the Attawapiskat mouth, not an inland confluence or lake terminal. The connecting channel is not named in this source reading and is not included as a separate selected FID.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern initial feeder and small lake sequence
correspondence.finding: The initial selected corridor lies in the unnamed lake-studded upland. Its northward feeder turns east and northeast through small elongate lakes and a mapped rapids reach. The observed geography supports this bounded headward portion without assigning the downstream river name to it.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported bounded headward corridor; unnamed.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Overby Lake sheet transition into the broad northwest-oriented corridor
correspondence.finding: The small feeder reaches a broader lake/river corridor that continues northwest across the sheet boundary. Its broad setting and lake passage are visible, although a bold sanctuary boundary overlaps much of the central watercourse. These observations do not independently establish a uniform name or all subsequent drainage links.
correspondence.correspondence: Bounded lake/corridor observation; no downstream name propagation.

correspondence.component_scope: Western middle lake chain and its material northeastward connection
correspondence.finding: The selected model follows the western sequence of elongate lakes and streams, then turns northeast toward the lower north-flowing river west of Brichta Lake. Much of the west-side sequence is visible, but the material connection across the sanctuary-boundary overprint cannot be established as a continuous, unambiguous hydrographic link from the source pixels read.
correspondence.correspondence: Material connector unresolved; this is more than a missing name on an otherwise completed route.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern named headwater reach and middle river west of Brichta Lake
correspondence.finding: An eastern headwater reach bears the Tingmeak River label and leads toward the northward lower course. The selected path uses the western approach instead of this labelled eastern headwater reach. The downstream river corridor west of Brichta Lake is visible, with lateral tributaries and adjacent lakes. Brichta Lake is not assigned as a selected through-lake merely because it is nearby.
correspondence.correspondence: Partial middle/lower river identity; relationship to selected western feeder still depends on the unresolved connector.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Tingmeak River and southern Elu Inlet sheet continuation
correspondence.finding: The mapped river continues from the northern central sheet into the southern part of Elu Inlet sheet, then runs generally north and northeast across low tundra with small lakes and tributaries. The Tingmeak River label is on this lower corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported bounded lower-course geographic and historical cartographic-name correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal terminal east of Dease Point
correspondence.finding: The selected lower approach reaches the small branched coastal inlet east of Dease Point on Queen Maud Gulf. Kuugaarjuk River is separately depicted immediately to the west. The observed terminal is coastal rather than an inland lake; no precise contemporary outlet branch or endpoint is claimed.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported actual terminal setting at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern headward tributary and Los Pavos corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected headward section is in the low limestone hills and seasonally wet depressions of Calakmul, west of Centauros del Norte. It follows the northward Los Pavos approach toward the San José (Kilómetro Ciento Veinte) road-crossing sector. The selected initial feeder is not given a separate established name.
correspondence.correspondence: Full headward corridor read at generalized component scale; no precise spring, vertex or permanent-flow claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Pozas branch and Desempeño junction
correspondence.finding: North of the road-crossing sector the selected route corresponds to the Las Pozas arm, which bends west to join the separately mapped Desempeño approach. It then continues north through the flood-prone drainage east of the Xbonil lake corridor. The western Desempeño approach is a separate feeder, not the selected southern headward path.
correspondence.correspondence: Material upper branch choice and joining route are read on the original connected-drainage map; labels are not propagated across exact unmarked transitions.

correspondence.component_scope: Arrigueña and the Yohaltún–Edzná drainage connection
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation follows the Arrigueña corridor northwest through the Chilam Balam and Yohaltún setting, then north toward Nayarit de Castellot (Xnohá). The mapped drainage and canal network connects across the Yohaltún–Edzná lowlands to the Champotón head near San Juan Carpizo. Both original basin maps and the hydraulic-infrastructure map show this material connection; the prose explains the seasonal southern tributary supply and agricultural drains.
correspondence.correspondence: Full intervening corridor and drain/river connection read. Seasonal drainage and artificial channels are retained as distinct types of passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower named river through Canasayab, Ulumal and Moquel
correspondence.finding: The named lower river runs west from the San Juan Carpizo area, past Canasayab and Ulumal, then bends north toward Moquel and the coast. This is the lower portion of the selected route. The source treats the named Champotón as a much shorter river than the retained model mainstem, rather than extending its name through every southern tributary and drain.
correspondence.correspondence: Named lower-river correspondence established from original maps and bounded primary prose.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected terminal corresponds to the Champotón river mouth at the town of Champotón on the Gulf of Mexico. It is a direct coastal outlet, not a termination in Laguna de Términos or one of the inland lakes.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal setting read at ordinary generalized coastal scale; no exact modern bank or mouth-point claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake and reservoir scope
correspondence.finding: Silvituc, Chama Há and Xbonil are mapped in connected or adjacent western drainage corridors. The selected southern Las Pozas/Los Pavos arm does not require a through-crossing of these named lakes. The reviewed route passes wet lowlands and drains; no named reservoir crossing is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Material lake context distinguished from the selected channel; adjacent lake names are not assigned to selected reaches.
